title: Knowledge item (knowledge/<module>/<kind>/<ID>.yaml)
description: One fact the project knows about itself — a requirement, a business rule, a domain term, an architecture note, an API, a DB model, an ADR, a task, or a test (T61). Every kind shares one envelope so a query can cross kinds; only `payload` differs, discriminated on `kind`. One item per file: two people editing different items edit different files, so git merges them without a conflict. The file is the source of truth — nothing derives an index from it, because a stored derivation is a second source of truth waiting to disagree with the first.

schema_version.description: Generation of this envelope. Bumped only when a change would break an existing reader.

id.description: The id space is the one the pipeline already uses (T19): REQ-/DES-/BE-/FE-/TEST- and ADR-NNN. Deliberately not a parallel id — a knowledge id that differed from the id in plan.md would need a mapping nobody maintains. The prefix must match `kind`; that pairing is checked in knowledgeModel.ts, not here, because JSON Schema cannot express 'BE- or FE-, but only for kind task' without nine more branches.

kind.description: Which of the nine entity types this item is. Also picks the payload branch below.

title.description: One line a person can recognise the item by in a listing. Never empty — an item nobody can identify in a list is one nobody will find.

body.description: Prose. May be empty when the payload IS the content (a domain term, a DB model), which is why it is required-but-emptiable rather than optional: a reader never has to ask whether the key is missing or the text is.

repo.description: Which repo of a multi-repo workspace (T42) this belongs to. null = the single/primary repo. A label only — it does not say where knowledge/ itself lives.

module.description: The _docs/module/<name>/ delivery unit this belongs to. null = project-wide (an ADR, a domain term the whole project shares).

owner.description: The role answerable for this item (T65). The ten pipeline stages plus human — the same AgentStage set the orchestrator already routes on, not a second role vocabulary.

status.description: draft = written, nobody has checked it. reviewed = someone read it. approved = binding; downstream work may rely on it. deprecated = superseded or withdrawn, kept because something still cites it.

sensitive.description: True when this item touches auth, personal data, payments, uploads, or untrusted input — the same trigger as plan.md's Security gate. Read as a query filter here; T68/T69 build field-level policy on it.

version.description: Bumped by exactly 1 every time the content changes. Two people editing the same item both bump the same line, so git reports a conflict on `version` itself instead of silently merging two different edits — that is the mechanism, not bookkeeping.

sources.description: Where this knowledge came from (T62/T72). At least one, always: an item with no source is an assertion nobody can check, which is the exact failure requirement.md's References table already exists to prevent.

relations.description: Outgoing edges only. The reverse index is built in memory by knowledgeBase.ts, the way TaskGraph builds its incoming map — storing both directions would be two records of one fact, free to disagree.

payload.description: The kind-specific half. Which branch applies is decided by `kind` below.

type.description: What kind of thing was read. `human`/`agent` are first-class: a fact someone stated in an interview is a real source, and pretending otherwise is how it ends up looking like a fact from a file.

locator.description: Where exactly: `path#L10-L24`, a table name, an OpenAPI path, a person's name, a role name.

captured_at.description: When the source was read — deliberately not `updated_at`. An item edited today from a file read six months ago is stale in a way `updated_at` cannot show. T71 reads this one.

digest.description: Hash of the slice that was read, so a later run can tell the source changed underneath. null when the source cannot be hashed (a person, a conversation).

source_id.description: The raw source in knowledge/_sources/ this was read from (T62). Optional because a source ref can name material nobody registered — but when it is set it must resolve, and that is what makes provenance answerable (T72) rather than merely recorded.

type.description: Which kinds may sit on each end is a matrix enforced in knowledgeModel.ts — a graph where anything may point at anything degenerates into a flat list with arrows, and check() could not then say what is wrong.

to.description: Id of the target item. Checked for existence by check(), not here — during discovery knowledge arrives in batches, and a target not written yet is reported rather than thrown on.

assumption_unconfirmed.description: CLAUDE.md's rule made machine-readable: a number nobody sourced is an assumption, in writing. True here is what the Thai marker for an unconfirmed assumption says in requirement.md.

enforcement.description: Where the rule is actually held. `manual`/`unknown` are honest answers — a rule believed to live in code but actually living in someone's head is the drift T66 exists to flag.

contract_name.description: The same string a plan task names in `produces`/`consumes` (taskGraph.ts). One name on both sides is what lets an ordering edge be derived instead of remembered.

relations.description: Prisma-level relations as written in design.md's Data Model. Prose on purpose — this mirrors the contract, it does not replace schema.prisma, and design.md still wins if the two disagree.

plan_status.description: plan.md's Status cell (T52). Only qa-engineer ever writes `verified`/`blocked`; the owning engineer may set `in_progress` on its own row.

orchestrator_task_id.description: PersistedTask.taskId — the join between this graph and the state machine. null for a task the orchestrator never ran.

automated.description: False is the normal value — tests are opt-in per CLAUDE.md and usually absent. It says the level was decided, not that a suite exists.
